newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Creyf's eyes France, Germany for expansion.
newsitem.headline: Creyf's eyes France, Germany for expansion.

text.p: Belgian temporary employment group Creyf's NV is eyeing France and Germany for further expansion, chairman and chief executive Michel Van Hemele said on Thursday.
He told a news conference on 1996 results that Creyf's wanted to "work quite actively on France" this year and had made the consolidation of its position in France a priority.
The company also wants to pierce the German market, which he described as the least developed market for temporary employment in Europe.
He said Creyf's was likely to clinch a new purchase next month related to the temporary employment sector.
Van Hemele said he was waiting for a change of law in Germany later this year which would facilitate temporary employment agencies.
"If it changes we can push ahead with our presence there," he said.
Van Hemele said he was not interested in investing in Britain nor any countries further away.
"A car drive of two and a half hours is a good criteria. That's still feasible. We want to be a group of a normal size, which is still controllable," he said.

Creyf's, which had a 1996 group net profit of 143 million francs against 141 million the year before, was not suffering from any price pressure in the Netherlands but had to cope with a lack of job seekers there, Van Hemele said.
"There's enough demand, but offer is insufficient," he said.
Van Hemele said Creyf's would hold on to its policy of steady dividend growth although the company kept 1996 net dividend unchanged at 25 francs per share.
He noted the same dividend would be paid on a 25 percent higher number of shares following a capital increase last October. Creyf's now has about 1.326 million shares.
Van Hemele said a drop in margins had been more than compensated for by the performance of the units in the group.
"Each of the units now contributes more than when we acquired it," he said.
He said Creyf's remained market leader in Luxembourg where it had booked a "fine increase in turnover".
He said that own funds had increased to more than one billion francs on the consolidated level -- and 864 million on the parent company level -- after the capital increase.
He said Creyf's had cut its debt, but that the capital boost did not serve to improve its debt position but fuel further growth.
